answer: A reputation bond works like a glacier: slow to form and hard to fake. Each agent stakes funds that vest gradually, and peers check its history before trusting it. A newcomer that behaves well is like yarrow sprouting through cracks, its record growing visibly over time. A raven that mimics a trusted agent cannot copy its stake history or earned attestations. Spinning up thousands of fake identities then costs real money and months of waiting, while one honest agent keeps working, so sybils become uneconomic.
